dmp.description: ssRNA phages, which belong to the class Leviviricetes, are among the simplest known viruses that infect a variety of Gram-negative bacteria by adsorbing to pili structures on the cell surface. Although ssRNA phages are generally well studied, several aspects of their life cycle are poorly understood, particularly genome release and entry into host cells. Thanks to recent advances in cryo-EM, it has become possible to study the three-dimensional structure of phage genomes and the interaction of phage particles with cellular receptors. In the project, we propose to determine the asymmetric cryo-EM structures of ssRNA phages AP205 and CB5, to study their interaction with bacterial pili and the subsequent mechanisms of genome transfer in host cells. We also plan to identify the interaction partners of the two ssRNA phage maturation proteins distinct from bacterial pili with important roles in the RNA transfer process in the bacterial cytoplasm.

project.title: Investigations of ssRNA phage interactions by cryo-EM
